page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.8-32 is an x86_64 compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by AMD EPYC 9J45 processors clocked at 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs via dedicated allocation, providing two execution threads per core. System memory totals 32.0 GB, resulting in an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU and a tight 1:2 core-to-memory distribution suited for CPU-heavy tasks.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, operating purely on network-attached remote block storage for persistence and file system demands. Similarly, it lacks discrete GPU acceleration, keeping the host design concentrated on standard CPU tasks. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the absence of bundled NVMe storage and GPU coprocessors provides an economical computing profile for operations requiring dedicated processor resources without the overhead of unused accelerator or storage silicon.

This hardware balance makes the VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.8-32 appropriate for compute-oriented application tiers, continuous integration and build automation pipelines, batch transcoding tasks, and API microservices that do not depend on large in-memory caches.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.8-32 is a compute-aligned virtual machine within the Standard family, driven by AMD EPYC 9J45 processors operating at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 8 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading to deliver 16 vCPUs alongside 32 GB of system memory. Operating at a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration is oriented toward workloads requiring steady processor throughput rather than high memory allocations. The instance includes no integrated local storage, requiring attached remote block volumes for persistence, and does not feature GPU acceleration. Network access is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address. By delivering dedicated core allocations without bundling expensive local NVMe or accelerator hardware, the shape offers an efficient compute-per-core footprint. VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.8-32 is well suited for compute-focused workloads, including build systems, microservices backends, batch processing, and horizontally scaled web serving.
